methodological_questions: How is offensive reorganization measured relative to baseline L, and is L defined before outcomes are observed?
Can the association between reorganization and change in points per possession be tested with 148 spells at useful power?
What minimum detectable rho applies to the spell-level test?
Which measurement, selection and confounding risks affect spell-level analyses built from play-by-play data?

historical_evidence.finding: On/off identity displacement D_A, shaper vs usage-matched role occupant. Recorded: 908 player-seasons with >=400 possessions on and off; 96 usage-matched pairs (caliper 0.03). Delta D_A=+0.115, t=6.35, p~7e-9, shaper larger in 81% of pairs; Delta D_pi=+0.011 p~1e-4; r(L,D_A)=+0.60 (shapers +0.79). Validation status recorded as 'no_validation_recorded; evidence: NOT_RECORDED'.

Offensive-identity resilience: connector absence vs usage-matched others. Recorded: unmatched connector vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97 p=2.87e-08; usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35 p=7.35e-09, n=96; vs terminal +0.0777, t=2.37, p=0.0261, n=25. Limitations recorded: LIM:small_sample; risks MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Absence validation (structure moves under real absence; simulation tracks it). Recorded sub-results: [APPA-006] V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]. [APPA-007] V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] FAIL; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115 FAIL. Limitation recorded: LIM:small_sample.

Fragility confirmatory: F1a usage decoupling and F1b split-half stability of residual influence. Recorded: F1a cosine R2=0.094, residual-share 0.906 PASS; F1b pooled-residual rho=+0.685 p=0.0000; usage-partial rho=+0.557. Limitation recorded: LIM:low_measurement_reliability; risk MEASURE_RELIABILITY.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Validating that the LOO simulation predicts the magnitude of real absence-driven structural change (V2a, V2b).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as FAIL with CIs spanning zero (V2a rho=+0.288, p=0.077; V2b partial rho=+0.253, p=0.115); the record carries LIM:small_sample and an overall status of untestable. The structural-movement part (V1) did pass.

failed_approaches.what_failed: No failure recorded; the family is a positive result. Its recorded limitations (small sample, mechanical floor) bound how strongly the result can be read.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failure mechanism: D_positive (no failure). Recorded limitations: LIM:small_sample; RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR; RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work by these records measured absence-driven identity displacement (D_A) and found that connector or shaper absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched controls (FAM:SF-PAP-014, FAM:SF-APPS-088).
Within those records, the baseline-type measure L correlates with displacement (r(L,D_A)=+0.60, FAM:SF-PAP-014), which supports the idea that L captures absence-related structural change.
Real absences move association structure (V1 passed in FAM:SF20), but the simulation-magnitude link (V2) did not pass with the recorded sample.
Earlier project work has used absence spells and usage-matched pairs as a design, with n=96 pairs in the displacement analyses.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records measures change in points per possession. The outcome in this question has not been studied in any returned record.
The retrieved records do not define reorganization relative to L in the way this question uses it, so the association between reorganization and PPP change is not shown.
The retrieved records do not give a power analysis for a spell-level rho with 148 spells, and do not report the MDE the question cites.
No retrieved record tests whether the L-to-outcome association holds in playoffs, in 2025-26 data, or after controlling for minutes and usage of the teammates who play more.
own_inferences: Adjacent evidence supports the measurement logic (L tracks displacement), but this is not a test of PPP change. The question needs its own outcome definition.

A rough MDE for Pearson/Spearman rho at alpha 0.05 two-sided, 80% power and n=148 is about 0.23 (approximation z-based: (1.96+0.84)/sqrt(145)). Effects smaller than about 0.2 would not be reliably detected. This is my calculation, not a recorded result.
Given that the usage-matched design used 96 pairs and reported large effects, a spell-level PPP-change test with 148 spells probably has adequate power only for moderate-to-large associations.
The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are complete as of 2026-11-01 (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21), so the data version is fixed for this test.
uncertainties: 'Reorganization relative to L' is not defined in the task statement; the metric, the baseline L, and the window for measuring PPP change are all unspecified.
The unit 'n=986' is not identified; it is unclear whether it is spells, player-seasons or possessions.
The validation status of SF-PAP-014 is recorded as NOT_RECORDED, so its displacement measure has not been independently validated.
Retrieval returned no record that computes change in PPP, so the outcome's behaviour and noise level in this data are unknown.
Whether L is computed from information that includes the absence window (leakage) is not stated in the retrieved records.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence showed that L relates to identity displacement (FAM:SF-PAP-014, r=+0.60) and that absence designs with usage-matched controls are workable (FAM:SF-APPS-088). That made a test of the L-based construct reasonable, so I did not reject the question outright. It also showed that the closest outcome-level test (FAM:SF20 V2) failed under small samples, and that the matched designs rest on 96 pairs with recorded small-sample and mechanical-floor risks. Those findings led to proceeding only with changes: define L and the outcome before analysis, pre-specify the spell-level test, and report the MDE rather than assume power.

blocking_constraints.text: With 148 spells the rho MDE is about 0.23 (own approximation). Smaller associations cannot be reliably detected, and FAM:SF20 V2 failed on a small sample.
Reorganization and PPP change both come from the same play-by-play and derived possession records, so the outcome and predictor may share construction artefacts.
If L or the reorganization measure uses possessions after the absence window, the association can be inflated. This must be ruled out in the definition.

prior_work.summary: Earlier records show that absence displaces team offensive identity, that L correlates with that displacement, and that real absences move association structure. None of them measures change in points per possession or the reorganization-to-PPP association asked here. The question is therefore only partly answered by adjacent work. The SF20 V2 outcome-level test failed under small samples.

risks.text: 148 spells give limited power for a rho test; the MDE is about 0.23 by my approximation, and the adjacent SF20 magnitude test failed on a small sample.
Recorded for FAM:SF-APPS-088: a floor effect in the displacement measure may inflate or distort results when baseline structure is weak.
Recorded for FAM:SF18 as low measurement reliability; a noisy reorganization measure attenuates any PPP association toward zero.
Absences are not random (injury, rest, trades). Spells selected on large prior reorganization or PPP swings will regress toward the mean, creating spurious associations.

Minutes, usage, opponent quality, and the playoff vs regular season setting can drive both reorganization and PPP change. Usage-matching was used in the adjacent records but must be re-specified here.
L must be fixed before the absence window and before PPP change is measured; any post-absence information in L inflates the association.
Both predictor and outcome are derived from play-by-play possession records, risking shared-construction correlation.
Partial possessions and sparse per-spell possession counts can make PPP change noisy, especially in short spells.
Multiple reorganization metrics, windows and baselines tried against PPP change would inflate false positives unless pre-registered.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 and playoff data mixes eras and rotation regimes; the association may not be stable across them.
A placebo or null-absence comparison is needed; without one, the association may reflect generic variability in reorganization rather than absence.

design.estimand: Association (Spearman rho, plus OLS slope with CI) between reorganization of offense relative to baseline L and change in points per possession across absence spells, with L fixed before the absence window.
design.unit: Absence spell (one player absence episode for one team), with the reorganization measure and PPP change computed within the spell window.
design.sample: 148 spells as recorded, drawn from NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are complete by 2026-11-01. Report n=986 units separately if they are a different unit; this is not specified in the task.
design.power: Report MDE for rho at alpha 0.05, 80% power, n=148 (about 0.23 by approximation); state that the test is powered only for moderate-to-large associations. Report achieved CI width.
design.controls: Pre-specify minutes, usage and opponent strength; match or adjust for usage using the usage-matched design of FAM:SF-APPS-088/FAM:SF-PAP-014; include a placebo window with no absence; exclude spells with too few possessions.
design.falsification: Placebo spells with no absence should show no association; a shuffled L should yield null; if the association disappears under usage matching, treat as confounded.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary metric and baseline L; treat alternative metrics as secondary with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary rho is positive with CI excluding zero after controls and passes the placebo check; rejected if the CI is tightly around zero with the MDE stated; otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-11-01: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the version and record the date.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
